chunks: And as for what was narrated - Musa ibn al-Qasim from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the person in ihram who says 'No, by Allah' and 'Yes, by Allah' while he is truthful to it, is there anything (penalty) upon him? He said, 'No.' The meaning is if it happens once or twice. But if he exceeds that, then the kaffarah (expiation) is obligatory upon him according to what we have previously mentioned.
And as for the dispute (jidal), it is the saying of the one who says 'No, by Allah' and 'Yes, by Allah' (repeatedly/excessively). Narrated.

key_terms.الْجِدَالُ: Dispute, argumentativeness, or excessive swearing used in debate
key_terms.الْكَفَّارَةُ: Expiation or penalty for a religious violation
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: The person in the state of ihram (pilgrimal consecration)

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for a pilgrim in ihram who repeatedly swears 'No by Allah, Yes by Allah'?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Musa ibn al-Qasim via Yunus ibn Ya'qub, distinguishing between simple truthful affirmation and the contentious 'jidal' that triggers expiation. This highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on intent and frequency, where mere repetition while truthful incurs no penalty, but excessive or argumentative swearing violates the sanctity of the ihram state. The text underscores the precision required in distinguishing between casual speech and deliberate transgression during pilgrimage rituals.
